title: The wire: workflows types
description: Part of the source of every type on the wire (#1135, #5380): one file per domain in Packages/Wire/schema. A $ref to another file names it (core.schema.json#/definitions/JSONValue); scripts/wire.sh gen reads them all.

reason.description: Why the person declined, in their words (#4039): only with decline or cancel. The agent reads it.

deadline.description: When the wait ends if its sessions have not (#5152; was checkAgainAt).

BusDelivery.description: bus/deliver (#4729): one event on the bus that matched subscriptions of this machine, and which ones. Best effort: usually once, sometimes never, rarely twice.

BusEvent.description: An event on the bus (#4729, spec 4724-event-bus, "The bus"): its envelope, and its data sealed to the person's machines (#4825). The control plane reads only refs, names and times (principle 7, #4726) and opens no sealed copy; a machine with no copy of its own reads the subject's state now, by its ref.

specversion.description: The CloudEvents version of the envelope (#4728, spec 4724-event-bus, "An event"): always "1.0".

id.description: The event's ref (#4728): the subject's ref, "@", the type, and, when the same type can happen again to that thing, "/" and the provider's key for this one, such as github:pr:alexec/agents#4702@pr.commented/2457. It comes from the provider's data only, never from the machine or the clock, so two machines make the same id for the same happening.

type.description: The event's type, noun.verbed (#4728): the same as name, which stays for one release.

provider.description: Who the event is about (#4728): github, jira, slack and so on; agents for the app's own events; server:<name> for an MCP server's event that says no subject.

topic.description: The provider's space (#4728, spec 4724-event-bus, "Topics"): a repo's full name, a Jira project, a Slack channel; the project or the machine for the app's own events. Lower case; can be empty.

subject.description: The ref of the thing the event happened to (#4728). None for an MCP server's event that says no subject.

source.description: provider:topic, as CloudEvents asks for one (#4728).

time.description: When it happened, in RFC 3339 (#4728): the provider's own time when it says one.

producer.description: The machine that raised it (#4728), as agents:machine:#<machine>. Not part of the event's identity.

sealed.description: The event's data (at most 256 KB), sealed by the machine that raised it to each machine of its person's lock (#4825). In bus/deliver, only the copy for the machine it goes to. None when the data is larger, or the machine has no lock.

poll.description: The producer lease of the poll that made it (#4731), when a machine polled a server for it: a hash of the folder's project, the server's name, the event and its filters, the same on every machine. The control plane delivers it to the machines that stand by on that poll. Not part of the event's identity.

BusLease.description: bus/lease (#4731, spec 4724-event-bus, "The bus", step 6): the polls a machine is about to make, at most 100, each asking for its producer lease or renewing it, and the leases it lets go (its Mac goes to sleep, a subscription ended). The control plane gives each lease to one machine at a time, for 5 minutes from its last renewal.

polls.description: The polls' keys (BusEvent.poll), each 1 to 128 bytes.

release.description: The keys of the leases this machine lets go. One another machine holds is left as it is.

BusLeased.description: bus/lease's answer (#4731): who holds each poll's lease now, in the order asked.

BusLogPage.description: bus/log's answer (#4732): envelopes of the caller's bus, newest first. Envelope only, as the bus keeps it: no data.

next.description: Where the next page back starts, as before; none when nothing older was read.

hasMore.description: Whether older envelopes are on the bus log.

BusLogQuery.description: bus/log (#4732, spec 4724-event-bus, "The bus log"): a page of the caller's bus log, newest first, narrowed by the envelope's fields.

before.description: The next of the page before: only envelopes older than it.

limit.description: At most this many; 100 when absent, never more than 500.

provider.description: Only events of this provider (#4732): github, jira, agents and so on.

type.description: Only events of this type (#4732), noun.verbed, or noun.* for every type of that noun.

topic.description: Only events on this topic (#4732), such as a repo's full name; lower case.

BusProducerLease.description: One producer lease (#4731): the machine that polls, until when, and whether it is the one that asked. A machine that is not the holder stands by: it does not poll, and the control plane delivers it what the holder's poll makes.

holder.description: The holder's machine id on the control plane.

BusPublish.description: bus/publish (#4729): events a machine recorded, at most 100 at a time, oldest first. Best effort: one not sent when it happened is never sent later.

BusPublished.description: bus/publish's answer (#4729): how many events were new on the bus, and how many were dropped as copies of one already on it (the same id).

BusSubscribe.description: bus/subscribe (#4729): every subscription of a machine, at most 1,000. It replaces the ones the machine sent before; an empty list ends them all. A machine sends it again after each connect, as the control plane keeps none across a restart.

BusSubscribed.description: bus/subscribe's answer (#4729): how many subscriptions the control plane holds for the machine now.

BusSubscription.description: One subscription on the bus (#4729): a wait or a workflow trigger of a machine. Each field that is there must match the event's envelope; one that is not there matches every event.

id.description: The machine's own name for it, sent back with each event it matches.

provider.description: The event's provider: github, jira, agents and so on.

type.description: The event's type, noun.verbed, or noun.* for every type of that noun.

topics.description: The topics it is about; none for every topic. Lower case.

subject.description: The one thing it is about.

ContentBlock.description: ContentBlock (ACP/ContentBlock.swift): the protocol's own block shapes, as sent. A block of a kind this build doesn't know is written back as it came, so any other `type` may arrive.

DeployCheckEvent.description: check.changed's details (#5262): the check, and what it is on: the deploy's ref when it is a deploy's check, and the target either way. component, environment and tier are the target's, flat, so a wait or a trigger can narrow by them.

DeployEvent.description: deploy.started, deploy.succeeded and deploy.failed's details (#5262), and deploy.waiting's beside its own: the deploy, and its target's component, environment and tier, flat, so a wait or a trigger can narrow by them (tier: production). outcome is deploy.failed's: failed or cancelled.

DriveApproval.description: Whether an agent's lease of the browser or the screen waits on a person (#4264). ask: each lease opens a Needs you request of kind approve (secretUse, use browser or screen), the default on a machine that a person uses; always: it never asks, the default on a machine that only agents use (a bot's machine, a Codespace), where ask counts as always, as nobody answers there; off: the tools are not offered, and are refused.

ElicitationHandOff.description: An agent's hand_to_person (#3529): one step the person does on the page in the machine's browser (solve a CAPTCHA, sign in). The form's one choice is Done or Can't do it; a client that can show the machine's browser offers Open the page, unless the step is in another window (window).

window.description: Where the person does the step when it is not in the machine's browser (#5095): one of the agents' own Chrome windows, as "the agents' Chrome (DevTools port 9233), at the tab “Create account”". A client then offers no Open the page and says this window instead.

provider.description: Only events of this provider (#4730): github, jira, agents and so on. With provider, topics or subject the pattern also hears the person's other machines' events, on the bus.

topics.description: Only events about one of these topics (#4730), lower case: a repo's full name, a Jira project, a Slack channel.

subject.description: Only events about this one thing (#4730).

debounce.description: Seconds (#4730): a burst of matches on one subject and type is held this long and delivered once, the last one, with how many came. Best effort.

EventPattern.description: EventPattern (Model/EventPattern.swift), as its encode(to:) writes it (073): `filters` holds every filter as one string, a list joined by `|` so an older build reads it as a value that never matches, and `anyOf` holds the lists whole. Read `anyOf` over `filters`.

forPerson.description: Only the connected person can carry this on (#3051): review.requested or issue.assigned today. Left out or false for everything else.

producer.description: This machine's producer ref (#4732), agents:machine:#<machine>, as its own events say it: an event whose producer is another says which machine raised it.

iterations.description: How many turns it took towards the goal, where the runtime counts them.

reason.description: Why it last stopped or paused, in the runtime's words.

tokenBudget.description: The tokens it can use on the goal, when it has a budget.

at.description: When the host last heard of it.

GoalStatus.description: Where a goal stands (#2742): active (it can drive more work, whether or not a turn runs now), paused, blocked, limited (a usage or token budget ran out) or complete.

KeepRequest.description: machines/keep: a request for a stopped host, kept until it is up. signed is the same request signed by the client (#3492, D6): a host that holds its person's lock takes only that, so the control plane keeps and delivers it as it is.

RemoveRequestList.description: people/removeRequests (#1002): the Remove requests waiting for an admin, oldest first.

RequestAnswer.description: One of the answers: form for a question, a secret or a step (#3863); checklist and approval for a forge item (#3865); secretUse for the use of a secret with Ask before use (#4015).

RequestApprovalAnswer.description: A needs-approval pull request's answer: approve adds approved, changes adds changes-wanted; the note is the person's comment on it.

RequestChecklistAnswer.description: The checklist's lines now ticked, by index. When every line is ticked, the request is answered.

RequestDeferral.description: When a deferred request comes back (#4233): at until, or when the person is next at the Mac (atMac: the Mac's presence changes from not here to here), whichever is first.

RequestDetail.description: The part of a request that depends on its source.

RequestFormAnswer.description: The answer elicitations/answer takes, for a question, a secret or a step.

RequestsDefer.description: Later (#4233): until, atMac or both; until is after now.

ResourceName.description: ResourceName (Model/Lease.swift): the name, trimmed and lower-cased, as a single string.

capacityWait.description: Why its line waits for the machine, not for a holder (#4579, #4748): "this Mac is near capacity", "this Mac is at capacity", or "this Mac has capacity again" while the line is served one a look. Only on a compute resource (capacity, build) with a free place and a line; absent otherwise and from a host from before #4748.

ResourceState.description: ResourceState (Daemon/DaemonAPI.swift), as its encode(to:) writes it (#116): every holder in `holds`, and the first again as `lease` for a reader from before counted holders. A host from before #116 sends only `lease`, so `holds`, `places` and `declared` may be missing.

TeamTrigger.description: workflows/trigger and workflows/fire (#2011, spec 736 FR-035): a folder or control-plane event (a server's, such as github or a channel's) or a schedule that a runs-on: workflow's trigger matched. A machine sends it to the control plane, which sends it once to one of the bot's machines. workflow is the folder's name and the workflow's id; trigger, the same words on every machine that heard it; event, the event (none for a schedule); dueAt, a schedule's due time.

TeamTriggerFired.description: workflows/fire's answer: ran is true when the machine took the trigger (it runs it, or records why not, as for any trigger); false when it cannot take it here (no such workflow, or runs-on: does not match this machine), and the control plane tries another.

TeamTriggerSent.description: workflows/trigger's answer: taken is true when runs-on: names a bot, and the control plane sends the trigger once to one of its machines; false when it names none, and the machine goes on as before.

TeamWorkflowRuns.description: One workflow a bot ran in the last 7 days (#1804, M6): how many times, and when last.

TeamWorkflows.description: console/teamWorkflows' answer (#1804, M6): every bot, for an admin.

continueWhenBack.description: `continue-when-back: true`: a run's turn refused for a spent allowance waits for it at once, as if the person had chosen Continue (#1918).

muted.description: `muted: true`: every run of the workflow starts muted (#2003), and muting or unmuting the workflow mutes or unmutes its runs.

runsOn.description: runs-on: (#1761, FR-034), which replaced hosts:: labels a machine must all have to run it: its id, its os (macos, linux), its provider, and its user's or bot's name. None runs on every machine of each person who turned it on.

WorkflowClaim.description: workflows/claimRun (#1761, FR-034): a machine asks to run a runs-on: workflow for one trigger. The first to ask wins; the trigger is the same words on every machine that heard it.

WorkflowClaimed.description: workflows/claimRun's answer: won is false when another machine runs it.

WorkflowHours.description: hours: (#4818): when a workflow may start, as the file says it. A fire outside it is held, and starts when it opens; Run now always runs.

between.description: As the file says it, "09:00-18:00"; it can go past midnight, "18:00-09:00". Absent is the whole day.

days.description: The days its window starts on. Absent is every day.

timeZone.description: time-zone:, an IANA name. Absent is the person's timeZone setting, else the host's zone.

named.description: hours: working or hours: not-working (#4821): the project's working hours (Folder.workingHours), or every time outside them. With it, between, days and timeZone are absent.

WorkflowHoursName.description: A named window in a workflow's hours: (#4821).

WorkflowLimitSettings.description: How many approved workflows may be turned on in each folder. An unset value means 20. The range is 1 to 100. Kept in workflow-limit.json.

hours.description: The first and the last hour of between:. The first is after the last when it goes past midnight (#4818): the hours after midnight belong to the day before.
The hours: to write (#4820): between:, days: and time-zone:. With no between: and no days: it takes hours: out, so the workflow may start at any time. Left out means left alone, as the cooldown is.

runsOn.description: runs-on: (#1761, FR-034), which replaced hosts:: labels a machine must all have to run it: its id, its os (macos, linux), its provider, and its user's or bot's name. None runs on every machine of each person who turned it on.

hearsFor.description: A bot's workflow that does not run here (#2027): the bot's name. This machine hears its server triggers with its own servers, once approved here, and sends each match to the control plane, which runs it on one of the bot's machines. Nothing of it runs here.

readyMadeUpdatedAt.description: When the daemon wrote a newer ready-made version over this unedited copy (#4071), for 7 days after it did.

newerReadyMade.description: An edited copy of a ready-made workflow whose ready-made version changed since the daemon made the copy (#4071): what the newer version changes. The daemon never writes over an edited copy.

hoursOpenAt.description: When a fire held outside the workflow's hours: can start (#4818): the first time its hours: are open once its cooldown is over. Absent while its hours: are open by then.

WorkflowSummary.description: Read forgivingly (Workflow.swift's init(from:)): a field that is missing or does not read takes its default (`isEnabled` true; false, 0, [] or absent for the rest).
